doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Boop-boop-de-doop and Invention for Guitar and Trumpet
summary: The origin of a title Kenton refused to announce, the Invention written for Maynard Ferguson and Sal Salvador that Holman dislikes, and the title Solo for Alto.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You‟re back with Stan Kenton. They resume again, the massive page after page of recording credits and broadcasts. I‟m looking at one here: NBC broadcast, Lincoln Park, Rhode Island, August 18, 1953, Boop-boop-de-doop, Bill Holman

Yeah, Boop-boop-de-doop. I just got that title from a rhythm of the bridge. It goes “boop boop-de-doop doo-be-doop doo-be-doop.” So I used that for a title. Stan – I told you he wouldn‟t say “Zoot.” He wouldn‟t go near “Boop-boop-de-doop.” In fact, we played it on several broadcasts from Birdland, and he made me get up and announce it every time.

Let me just backtrack a little bit, because I found in my notes two compositions: Invention for Guitar and Trumpet. The first entry that I saw for that was in September of ‟52. There are several entries. Again, all the live broadcasts. Then, Solo for Alto, which I presume was for Lee, maybe? Please tell us about those two.

The Invention for Guitar and Trumpet was one of the few assignments that Stan gave me at the time. He knew I was interested in lines and counterpoint and things like that. So he took the name of a contrapuntal form, which is the invention. He had Maynard to play high and Sal to play fast, and asked me to write the piece for them. I did. I don‟t like it at all. That‟s probably the worst chart I wrote for Kenton, and it‟s been recorded the most and re-released on this label and that label. It‟s coming back to haunt me all the time.
So, there it is. I‟m responsible.
Okay, then let‟s go on to Solo for Alto.
I don‟t know what that is. What‟s the date on that?
I have November 27th, 1952, NBC radio broadcast from New Jersey.

Yeah, that would have been Konitz, probably, but I can‟t remember. I‟ve run across that title before, and I can‟t remember what it is. We did several with him on All the Things You Are, which is his favorite tune of all time. He gave it different names, but I don‟t think Solo for Alto was one of them.
